## 2. Romantic but weird, and not slow

**Score:** 40
**Body:** Movie night with my girlfriend tonight and I'm stuck picking something. What we're after:

* Has romance in it, but not a conventional rom-com or a slow burn
* Doesn't drag : we don't want to be checking the runtime at the 40 minute mark
* A little strange. Surreal, offbeat, unsettling, dreamlike, whatever direction the weirdness goes

She really liked *The Dreamers*, *The lobster, I origins* so that's roughly the register we're aiming for , sensual, a bit claustrophobic, not playing by normal romance rules.

## 4. Looking for more dark psychological thriller/dramas

**Score:** 31
**Body:** Just finished American beauty for the first time and loved it. Looking for more psychological dramas similar to it. Gave same vibes as Donnie darko, perks of being a wallflower, dead poets society. I don’t really know how to describe these types of movies tbh but I always find them super interesting. 

### Top 10 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

1. one hour photo
2. The Machinist(2004)
3. The Game (1997)

Se7en (1995)

Zodiac (2007)

All from the same director. 
4. Mulholland Drive, The Butterfly Effect, Blue Velvet, The Killing of a Sacred Deer, Bugonia
5. Cure (1997)
6. Rear Window
7. Magnolia, from the same era; not a thriller but a drama

Jacob’s Ladder is you want something more Donnie Darko-ish and creepy

8. Citizen Kane (1941)!
9. Strange Days
10. American Beauty and Perks in the same list makes sense to me, you like movies about people quietly coming apart inside nice houses. Some that scratch that:

Little Children (2006). Probably the closest thing to American Beauty anyone made. Suburbs, bored adults, everybody making bad decisions, and it gets genuinely uncomfortable in the last act.

The Ice Storm (1997). A family in the 70s failing to talk to each other for two hours. Sounds like nothing, absolutely wrecks you.

Ordinary People (1980). If Dead Poets Society hit you, this one will too. A family after a death, and a parent who cannot fake being okay anymore.

## 5. Can you recommend movies like The Witch?

**Score:** 24
**Body:** I’ve never seen a horror movie that made me feel the same way The Witch did.

Honestly, no other movie has ever made me feel like the characters were truly facing Evil itself in the way that movie did. And it added a lot that, unlike in most horror movies where the characters suffer the consequences of a series of terrible decisions, the family hadn’t actually done anything to deserve what happened to them.

If anyone wants to recommend similar movies, feel free to do so below. I’ve already seen Longlegs, Oddity, Hokum, Apostle, Hereditary, and Midsommar, among others. The only one that gave me a similar feeling was The Blackcoat’s Daughter.

### Top 9 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

1. The original Wicker Man 
  - I watched it too and I really liked it. I feel Midsommar was inspired by it
2. Saint Maud (2019) if what you liked was the mix of religion, fanaticism, and supernatural ambiguity. It’s more psychological, but it shares that feeling of witnessing something deeply disturbing.  
  - Yeah second Saint Maud it doesn’t get enough love, great film
3. The Wailing (2016)

The Innocents (1961)
4. maybe Rosemary's Baby or The Ninth Gate
5. The Damned (2024)

EDIT: The Village (2004)
6. "The Medium" is what you're looking for.

"Exhuma" is one of my favorite films as well. It will leave you with that feeling you're looking for.

"The Wailing" (2016) is definitely in the same lane as what you want, too. It was just a tad bit hard for me to follow.

"Deliver Us" (2023) is a great, dark film. Begins with a gut punch lol

Lastly, "Leviticus" (2026) is a great film that came out this year. 
7. The Wailing (2016)  
  
When Evil Lurks (2023)

The Dark and the Wicked (2020)
8. The Shining made me feel exactly what you are describing. Like a malevolent force was overthrowing the characters.

## 2. Coyote vs. Acme Review

**Score:** 360
**Body:** Coyote vs. Acme is the long anticipated live action animated comedy that was never ever supposed to see the light of day on the big screen. Originally Warner Bros. Discovery was simply going to push the film to the side and use it as a tax write off and call it a day since they clearly had no faith in this film and thought that it would bomb at the box office. But, thankfully due to the backlash by fans, filmmakers and others within the industry Warner Bros. Discover reversed their decision allowing Director Dave Green to shop the film around to other distributors thus resulting in Ketchup Entertainment picking it up since they had also previously done so with The Day the Earth Blew Up. Coyote vs. Acme is an entertaining, goofy slapstick, heartwarming experience full of witty clever humor for adults and kids alike. It honors not just Wile E. Coyote and The Roadrunner but the entire catalog of Looney Tunes itself allowing these iconic characters to continue being preserved and flourish across generations. 

The story or plot of this film is pretty straightforward Wile E. Coyote after decades of trying to catch the Roadrunner is fed up after using every single trap and invention there is and failing every single time it is quite clear that the Acme Corporation is at fault for his failures and therefore should be sued for falsely advertising broken or faulty products. Coyote decides to get help from Kevin Avery, played by Will Forte, a loser dead beat lawyer whose firm always defaults to settling cases rather than fighting to win them. Kevin does not take Coyote’s case seriously in the slightest in his view it’s foolish to take on a big corporation like Acme and believes that cooler heads will prevail with his client Coyote which of course does not happen what transpires then is a team up of chaotic hilarity, fun, corporate corruption, and friendship. 

The casting in this film is great. Will Forte plays Kevin Avery to a tee. I love his interactions with Coyote and being a victim of physical slapstick violence and just being oblivious as to what is going on around him. Eventually, Kevin does get it together though and is not just some nimrod he actually cares and stands up for his clients. John Cena as Buddy Crane plays the perfect smug lawyer for Acme; he is ruthless, selfish, and arrogant as hell and we see that rivalry between him and Avery as they fight it out to see which side will win in the end. Eric Bauza plays Coyote but I love that Dave Green wanted to keep things old school with Coyote not relying on any dialogue. Coyote writing things out on signs or drawing to express what he’s saying is classic Coyote. I'm glad that they didn’t update the character at all because he is the star. It is his film after all making him speak probably wouldn’t carry that comedic charm that spectators recognize and love. 

It is hilarious and very self aware if you grew up with Looney Tunes and are a fan of Space Jam, Looney Tunes: Back in Action, Who Framed Roger Rabbit, Chip ‘n Dale Rescue Rangers, Coyote vs. Acme is totally for you! This film is NOT a cinematic masterpiece or a high concept big budget Hollywood film it will not generate a million or a billion dollars it will however, spark word of mouth and excitement for people who have waited for this to come out for years and finally support it! Coyote vs. Acme is a great time and I’m glad to have watched it at the cinema on my birthday. I highly recommend it. I definitely will plan on adding this film to my 4K Collection. A.

## 3. Is Deckard are terrible Blade Runner?

**Score:** 0
**Body:** Deckard is built up as the ultimate Blade Runner, so much so that he’s drafted in to take out these four new models. So when we see him in action we’ll see how badass this guy is at retiring these fuckers, right?  
  
Wrong.  
  
1) Zhora - she’s strangling him (because she saw through his phoney character act) and he’s utterly helpless and about to die… until a pack of groupies burst in and startle the bitch, allowing him to escape. He got *unbelievably* lucky.  
  
2) Leon - successfully sneaks up on Deckard starts beating seven shades of shit out of him and is about to gouge Deckard’s eyes… until Rachel miraculously appears and shoots Leon in the back of the head. Once again, Deckard is utterly useless and is saved by blind luck.  
  
3) Pris - OK he does take out Pris, but only after she sneaks up on him and nearly kills him. Again, he’s very lucky.  
  
4) Roy - Roy toys with Deckard and gets the better of him. Deckard is about to plummet to his death… until Roy has a miraculous change of heart and decides to save the guy trying to kill him. Once again, Lady Luck saves Deckard’s useless ass, and Roy dies before he can be ‘retired’.  
  
To add to his unprofessionalism, Deckard forces himself on Rachel. He’s supposed to kill these things not rape them 🤦🏻‍♂️  
  
I think it’s time we realised that Deckard is a shit cop, and maybe the worst Blade Runner on the force.

### Top 4 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

He's never portrayed as a genius, he's just the one guy who has made it to this point without getting his arms and legs ripped off. He's got dumb luck and a rat's survival instincts, that's why they give him the job.
  - >He's got dumb luck 

You got that right! His superpower is having a metric fuck-tonne of dumb luck.

That must be what Bryant meant by ‘I need your magic’


2. How many other Blade Runners do we know of? How many other replicants do we know of? Were their stories similar to those present in the first film? As in, were they all fueled by hatred and fear of death?
3. That’s the case with every other blade runner we’re presented with in the franchise. Replicants are cunning and physically imposing, desperate and violent people. We see the blade runner beef it in the opening and even K, a replicant blade runner with similar physical attributes gets his shit absolutely rocked throughout most of 2049.

Deckard raping Rachel is part of his character growth. They are still objects to him at that point, it stands to reason he’d treat them as such.

Batty’s mercy is the final puzzle piece to Deckard’s revelation. Replicants are human.
4. I just came across this interesting theory that possibly explains why Deckard is far less competent that his reputation suggests…

>  
Not only was Deckard a replicant in Blade Runner, he was a replicant implanted with the memories of Gaff (Edward James Olmos' character). Gaff was the real top Blade Runner, but was sidelined due to injury, hence the cane, and so Deckard was created to finish the job. This explains why Gaff seems to know what Deckard is thinking all the time, as illustrated by his origami figures, a chicken when he knows that Deckard is scared, a stick man with a boner when he is about to meet the smoking hot Rachael, and of course the unicorn at the end, showing that Gaff has specific knowledge of Deckard's recurring dream. It also explains the disdain that Gaff regards Deckard with, and adds meaning to the compliment he pays him at the end (after apparently hovering overhead without intervening even when Batty was about to kill Deckard). Gaff says "you've done a man's job," which from him would be the highest praise he could give a replicant.

## 4. Did Tarantino start the "perfect movie" trend?

**Score:** 0
**Body:** I remember seeing Tarantino on Jimmy Kimmel talking about his notion of a perfect film. "It may not be your cup of tea, but there's nothing you can say to bring it down." I think some of the films he mentioned were Back to the Future, Texas Chainsaw Massacre and Jaws.

Since then I see everyone, Letterboxd top-4ers, podcasters, critics, etc jostling to call a film "perfect".

Am I only just noticing it now, or did Tarantino start this all up?

### Top 6 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

1. Thank you OP proving how far this subreddit has truly fallen.

You are correct  that before Tarantino no one talked about a film being perfect or a film's quality  being outside of if you enjoyed it or not. 

Also you are correct that before Tarantino Letterbox  reviews never had anyone saying a movie is perfect  or not. 

And only time they are doing it in reference to Tarantino.


  - Lmao, it’s just observational but I’ve been noticing the quality of this sub sinking too. 

That said, I’ve always found the notion of a “perfect” movie as something alien. Art isn’t about perfection, perfection is a precise mathematical notion imho, it doesn’t really make sense to claim art as perfect as if there were one precise way that is the most correct to execute a thought or idea. 

Anecdotally, you can find “flaws” in several of the greatest films of all time, so even taking it with a grain of salt it seemed kind of a fools metric. For example, The Godfather has shoddy action beats, punches that clearly don’t connect, who gives a fuck about that? 
    - It’s a very recent notion that things or people have to be perfect or agreeable every single step of the way. God forbid something falters or hits a false note somewhere along the way.
2. You think Tarantino was the first person to describe a film as "perfect" and everyone else calling a film "perfect" is merely copying him? 

No-one else has described a film as "Perfect" before Tarantino?

Seriously? That's bizarre. 
  - More confusingly, that we somehow picked this up, as if by osmosis, from *Jimmy freakin Kimmel*.

The last time I seriously watched late night, Kimmel was on The Man Show.
3. I don't think so. I'd say people just for some reason often want new movies, books or games to be the best of all time whenever something comes around that they really like.

Seems almost the opposite of what Tarantino says, really. They really enjoyed it and right now it's what they fucking love. So... it's the best of all time. A maaasterpiece. It's like classic serial monogamy, where people always say their current partner is the real one, and all the other previous ones just lacked something. When really they may have really been perfect at that time in your life as well.

But simply put, I think this is a produce of a culture that is obsessed with rating and ranking art. It can't be great, it's gotta be perfect/better.
  - Yeah, I’ve noticed a lot of solid to good movies are almost being forced into masterpiece status due to vitality and recency bias, but they fail to stick in pop culture years later.
